reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse a COPY REPLACING whose pseudo-text-1 consists only of a separator comma or a separator semicolon (each a text word in 1985, so SR3 alone does not refuse it), while a comma beside another text word stays legal.

edition-consulted.switches: removal gate of the non-pseudo-text forms at 2023

reader.edition-search: the check (MatchWords excludes SeparatorCommaOrSemicolon; Count == 0 refused) consults no edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers ==;== (and is written in a form that needs --source-format free); ==,== and the comma-beside-a-word legal form were not exercised

probes.printed: error COBOL2572: COPY statement: pseudo-text-1 holds no text-word to match

probes.expected: legal: ==,W-A== holds a comma beside a word

citations.check: OK  §1985:XII.2.3 SR9  (2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR9

reader.notes: The separator comma and semicolon are scanned as their own kind and excluded from the match words, so a pseudo-text-1 of only those is refused with COBOL2572 at every edition. The message cites the 2023 rule number at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: Q9comma-001 (==, plus a comment line==), Q10semi-001 (semicolon and comma on two lines), Q12dbgcomma-001 (only a comma on a debugging line) all refused COBOL2572. Reading note: in ==,== the comma is followed by the closing delimiter, not a space; the compiler (and the reader) take it as a separator comma, which is the reading SR9 evidently intends (§1985:IV separator rule 6 lets a closing delimiter follow a comma); no decisive text against. cite.py: OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR9.
